mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where CPI YoY growth exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, which historically correlates with strong economic growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where UNRATE is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% MoM signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where HOUST MoM growth exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals a contraction in supply-side activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where INDPRO declines by more than 1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy combined with weak economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5% and GDPC1 YoY growth < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2pp in the same month, it signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals increased consumer spending and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of instances where RSAFS shows a sustained 3-month increase.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 2% YoY and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 3%, it signals strong supply-side growth with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of instances where INDPRO YoY growth > 2% and FEDFUNDS < 3%.
